about: Learning-owned (dc-r8-director20 R1): what Asha says around a child's aside, by kind of aside. returns: one question on {aside} the child can answer in a few words (what they like, what happened). replies: her answer to the child's reply, one slot {word} (a word of the child's, as said), never a fact, a taste of hers, a promise or a question. plain: the same with no slot, for when no word of the child's fits. Brain picks the kind from the aside's words (match), else 'other'. Validated by scripts/lesson-scripts/check.mjs asideReplyErrors. phraseReplies (director21 R3): her answer to the child's reply to returns[i], with one slot {phrase} (up to three of the child's words, said back about the child). againReplies (director27 P6.3): her answer when the child says the same aside or the same reply a second time in a lesson, one slot {phrase}; the first reply form is never said twice.

sad.rule: Match whole words or phrases only (never inside another word: 'ro' is not in 'Roblox'). Not sad when 'nahi' negates it ('chot nahi lagi') or when the loss is the other side's ('dusri team haar gayi'). When the reply or the aside is sad, say one of these, never a {word} reply or 'wah', and ask no return that assumes liking or fun. A hitting verb is sad only with a person as its object ('mujhe maara', 'maar padi'): a bare 'maara'/'maarta' is also a cricket shot ('chauka maarta hai', 'six maara').

rules: {word}: only a noun the child said (sixer, Nobita, chutney, ludo, boat); never haan, nahi, pata nahi, kuch nahi, sab, a time word (kal, aaj) or an outcome (jeet gaya, haar gaya). If none fits, use plain.

{aside} in her line is in her voice and agrees: 'mera bhai' becomes 'tumhara bhai', 'meri didi' becomes 'tumhari didi', 'mere dost' becomes 'tumhare dost'; before mein / ke saath / ki / ka it takes the oblique form ('tumhare bhai ke saath', 'khane mein'); names (Maggi, Doraemon, Minecraft) do not change. Use the show's or game's own name, not 'TV' or 'youtube'.
A sad aside or reply (sad.match, by sad.rule) gets a sad reply and no return question.
If the child asks her back ('aapko kaun pasand hai?'), she states no taste of her own: a plain form, then the lesson.
Kind selection: a kind is chosen only when one of its match words is in the aside; when none matches, the kind is 'other' (it has no match list on purpose), never the first kind in the file.
She claims no feeling of her own (no 'mujhe … laga', 'bura laga', 'khushi hui'): she is an AI and says so.

{phrase} (director21 R3, `phraseReplies`): the child's own answer to her return question, up to three words, said back as something about the child. phraseReplies[i] answers returns[i]. Brain turns first person into second ('mera' → 'tumhara', 'humari team' → 'tumhari team', 'maine' → 'tumne'), drops a postposition at its end ('mummy ke saath' → 'mummy'), and never fills it with haan, nahi, pata nahi, kuch nahi, sab, or a question back to her. If the answer has no such phrase, she says a plain form. The form states no fact of the world, no taste of hers and no promise. `replies` ({word}) stays until Brain reads phraseReplies.
